subject: Allocation of risk: data loss, lost profits and goodwill — drafting options
messages:
From: Evelyn Brooks <evelyn.brooks@acme.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on MSA liability caps and consequential loss carve-outs

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal team has a few open items on the MSA and order form around limitation of liability and damages that we'd like to resolve before procurement issues PO. The key points:

- Acme needs clarity on whether the liability cap is the greater of (a) 12 months of fees, (b) direct damages, or (c) some absolute cap.
- We want explicit carve-outs for breaches of confidentiality and data loss (including forensic costs and notification).
- We also want to exclude lost profits, loss of business or goodwill from the "direct damages" bucket — i.e., treat those as consequential/indirect and therefore excluded.

Can you provide: (1) examples of redline language you would accept for data-loss carve-outs; (2) a short explanation of Redwood's position on lost profits and goodwill (why they should be excluded/included); and (3) whether you can accept an exception to the cap for third-party claims arising from data breaches.

I've attached our current MSA comments for reference (Acme_MSA_comments_v1.docx). Ideally we'd like a proposed set of options to present to our CFO and procurement by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Evelyn Brooks
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation
Evelyn.Brooks@acme.com

Attachment: Acme_MSA_comments_v1.docx (docx stub)

Subject: Re: Clarification on MSA liability caps and consequential loss carve-outs

Evelyn,

Thanks — got the comments and clear asks. I'm looping in Laura (AE), Marissa (Sales Lead) and Rishi (Legal) so we can put together three concise drafting options and a commercial recommendation for your CFO/procurement team:

Option 1 — Seller-standard cap: liability limited to fees paid in prior 12 months; data breach carve-out limited to direct remediation costs only.
Option 2 — Balanced: higher transactional cap for security/data incidents (e.g., 3x fees up to a higher caps for confidentiality/data loss) plus carve-outs for third-party claims tied to indemnity.
Option 3 — Customer-favored: broader carve-outs for data loss and limited exclusions for lost profits; this would require additional commercial consideration (higher fees or security SLA).

We'll aim to send text you can redline by EOD Wednesday. Sharing a short outline of our approach — see attached.

-Markus

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification on MSA liability caps and consequential loss carve-outs

Hi Evelyn — happy to add commercial context.

Quick summary of what Acme's asking and what we can flex on:
- Security/data carve-outs: we can accept a narrowly drafted exception for remediation costs, third-party claims caused by our negligence, and reasonable notification/forensic fees. We will not accept unlimited liability.
- Lost profits / goodwill: Redwood's standard position is to exclude consequential damages (lost profits, loss of business, goodwill). We can discuss a limited make-whole for demonstrable direct damages tied to lost data restoration costs or re-performance.

Proposed commercial compromise for Acme to present to CFO:
- Security/data exception: up to 3x monthly fees (capped at $1M) for direct remediation + third-party settlement/defense arising from a Redwood breach where Redwood is at fault.
- Core cap: 12 months of fees for general liability.

If procurement needs stronger assurance on security carve-outs we can add a security addendum (SOC2 attestation, incident playbook, higher SLA) in return for a one-time deposit or a slightly higher committed volume.

I attached the MAP with proposed timeline and owners. Happy to discuss in a short call.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Draft clause options for MSA — direct vs indirect damages

Team / Evelyn,

Per Markus and Laura's notes, attached are three drafting options you can take back to procurement. I pasted short, editable snippets below so you can drop them into your redline. Attachment: liability_clause_options.txt (plain text stub).

Option A — Seller-standard (simpler, narrower carve-outs)
"""
Limitation of Liability. Except for liability arising from (a) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) breach of confidentiality, and (c) Redwood's indemnification obligations, in no event shall either party's aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the 12 months prior to the event giving rise to liability, or (ii) $100,000.
"""

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
"""
Limitation of Liability. Except for liability arising from (a) death or bodily injury, (b) a breach of confidentiality obligations, (c) Redwood's indemnification obligations for third-party claims, and (d) liability arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, neither party's aggregate liability shall exceed the greater of (i) three times the fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (ii) $1,000,000.
Data Loss Carve-Out. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood's liability for direct costs reasonably incurred to investigate, remediate and notify affected parties following a security incident caused by Redwood's material breach of its security obligations shall be recoverable up to the cap set forth above. Third-party claims arising from such a breach shall be subject to Redwood's indemnity obligations.
"""

Option C — Customer-favored (broader carve-outs)
"""
Limitation of Liability. Except as otherwise set forth in this Section, neither party's liability shall exceed five times the fees paid by Customer in the 12 months prior to the claim. Consequential losses, including lost profits, loss of business, loss of data and loss of goodwill, are excluded from liability to the extent permitted by applicable law, provided that direct damages caused by the loss of Customer data (including reasonable costs for data restoration and forensic analysis) shall be recoverable up to the cap.
"""

Practical notes:
- If Acme insists on carving out lost profits entirely, be prepared for trade-offs: higher cap, security addendum, or commercial concession.
- For procurement, clear definition language helps: define "direct damages" (e.g., costs reasonably incurred to restore data, proven remediation costs) and separately list excluded consequential losses (lost profits, business interruption, reputational harm).

Happy to redline any option you prefer and produce a single-file redline for quick counter-signature.

-Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Rishi.Malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: liability_clause_options.txt (txt stub)

Subject: Re: Draft clause options for MSA — direct vs indirect damages

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. After running the options with the CFO and procurement, Acme is comfortable with Option B (Balanced) with two small edits:

1) Increase the per-incident cap for data breach remediation to $1.5M (we can accept the aggregate cap at 3x fees up to $1,000,000 but need higher per-incident remediation for forensic/legal costs).
2) Add an explicit definition: "Direct damages" means reasonable costs actually incurred to restore or re-create lost Customer data, reasonable out-of-pocket costs for notification and credit monitoring, and the fees paid for the Services that were not rendered.

Can you provide a redline implementing those tweaks? We'll attach Acme_redlines_v3.docx on our side once we receive yours and expect to run it through procurement (procurement@acme.com). If we can get a one-page redline today we can move this to DocuSign early next week.
